claims.text: The homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy initially has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The initial FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent.
The initial alloy has high strength but is brittle.
Stress concentration at the incoherent interfaces causes the alloy's brittleness.
The proposed intervention is treatment in a hexahedron-anvil apparatus at approximately 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will transform the lamellar microstructure into a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
The HPHT-induced hierarchical microstructure will have coherent interfaces replacing the initial incoherent boundaries.
Coherent interfaces will facilitate dislocation transfer between the FCC and B2 phases.
Dislocation transfer between the phases will alleviate interfacial stress concentrations.
The hierarchical coherent microstructure will enable dislocation transfer, stacking faults, and twinning.
The activated deformation mechanisms will promote homogeneous strain distribution.
Homogeneous strain distribution will arrest interfacial cracking.
The resulting microstructure and deformation mechanisms will overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
The HPHT-treated sample will exhibit elongated cracks rather than isolated microcracks on its fracture surface.
At high strain, the GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge in the treated sample.
Convergence of FCC and B2 GND densities indicates strain homogenization.
Conventional thermal-mechanical treatments fail to produce the proposed hierarchical interface coherence.
Conventional thermal-mechanical treatments fail to produce GND homogenization.
Treatment below the required pressure-temperature window may fail to induce interface coherence.
Treatment above the required pressure-temperature window may cause phase instability.
